description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Tandem Diabetes Care develops medical devices and technology for people living with diabetes. The Embedded Software Engineer I contributes to the design, development, testing, troubleshooting, and documentation of software for the company’s medical devices.
Embedded Software Engineer I developing and testing medical-device software, supporting verification, validation, and design-control documentation

Responsibilities:
• A team member contributing to the design, troubleshooting, documentation, testing and debugging of software for the Company’s medical devices
• Develops, modifies, and tests software units per corporate software process documents
• Contributes to software design specifications, interface descriptions, and other software documentations; may act as documentation owner for limited scope projects
• Contributes to software validation (write, dry run & review) & verification protocols
• In coordination with the Software Test team, participates in formal test execution
• Assists with developing unit tests
• Embraces the Design Control process by participating in design reviews and maintaining design history files
• Supports software testing with utility software or special purpose embedded software
• May lead projects of limited scope
• Assists with training of new team members
• Manages source code effectively using Source Code Management (SCM) tools, processes, and procedures
• Assists product development engineers in the diagnosis and replication of build and deployment issues
• Researches new technologies as needed
• Attends and may coordinate documentation for the Software Review Board (SRB)
• Assists in analyzing returned products to determine root cause of failure
• Collects process metrics and lessons learned, reviews, and evaluates processes and work products and recommends improvements as appropriate
• Confirms completion of required training plan before assuming job responsibilities
• Ensures compliance with company policies, including Privacy/HIPAA, and other legal and regulatory requirements
• Other responsibilities as assigned

Requirements:
• Able to effectively convey information related to work product in one-on-one conversation or in a group
• Able to work effectively in a team environment
• Able to alter behavior and opinions in light of new information
• Able to assert own ideas and persuade others through effectively consolidating, evaluating, and presenting relevant information
• Experienced with MS Office
• Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Computer Sciences or related field or equivalent combination of education and applicable job experience
• Six months experience in the field of embedded software for medical devices or in a related area
• Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S
• We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time

Preferred:
• Some knowledge of Good Documentation Practices (GDP) preferred
• Exposure to formal software test methodologies preferred
• For Embedded Software Engineers: experience in the “C” programming language preferred
